name: Dual-Cell DDA Raycasting for Particles
definition: A ray-tracing mode (rt=on) where 30% of particles are glossy black mirrors and 35% are glass (IOR 1.5, Fresnel). Glass refracts through the sphere and exits the far side. The remaining particles are matte grey. The ray walk uses the fluid's own neighbour grid (sorted positions, sorted indices, cell offsets) with a 3D DDA over dual cells.
summary: Dual-Cell DDA Raycasting is a real-time ray-tracing optimization for particle volumes that uses a 3D DDA over dual cells to efficiently test for ray-sphere intersections, enabling glossy mirrors and refractive glass rendering.
